title: Claude can make and edit pictures and videos in Photonz through an MCP server and a skill
goal: Photonz comes with an MCP server and a Claude skill that teaches Claude to use it, so a person can ask Claude in plain words to build a video montage from their history, draw an icon, mark up an open screenshot, or rebuild a website's design system, and Claude does all of it in the app with every tool the app has. Claude can also see the picture or video exactly as it currently stands, so it can check its own work and correct it.
notes:
The user's words (2026-10-19, intake): 'i want an mcp server support and a claude skill to use it accompanying photonz. I'd like to be able to use claude to create and manipulate images and videos.' Their four scenarios are quoted in the acceptance. 'Consider that we'd want to have access to all of the tools, but also the model might need to access the image as it currently is for evaluation or validation.'

Existing thinking: docs/design/creation-vision.md:85-102 (the command API is the contract; the MCP server is the frontier path; schema-checked undoable commands are the safety rail; never couple to one model). Objective epic agent-drivable with children agent-api, agent-mcp, agent-skills was staged 'later' with no tasks; this task is why it is now 'now' (agent-ask stays later). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/agent.html.

What exists to build on, not confirmed in depth: the document model is pure Codable Swift in PhotonzCore (good for a structured read); DocumentRenderer in PhotonzRender renders offscreen; SVGExporter (Sources/PhotonzRender/SVGExporter.swift); VideoExporter and DocumentMovieWriter (Sources/PhotonzMedia); FeatureCatalog (Sources/PhotonzCore/FeatureCatalog.swift) may already list the app's features and could seed the coverage test; EditorCommands.swift; History.perform is the only mutation path (CLAUDE.md invariant). The playtest harness (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift, PlaytestScript in Core) already drives the probe app from JSON, but it is compiled out of release and works by clicking controls by name, so it is a reference for reaching app state, NOT the server's transport: the MCP must work in the shipping app and must not depend on control names (a locked screen takes those away, see CLAUDE.md).

Traps: (1) Do not build the server as a headless re-implementation that edits document files behind the app's back; the user wants to watch it happen in the open document and undo it. (2) Recommended zooms already exist for recordings (EditorState+Zoom.swift, ZoomLane.swift); reuse that, do not invent a second zoom picker. (3) Scenario 4 depends on Library components (ui-building epic); if components cannot yet be made from outside the UI, that is a gap to file, not to fake with flat pictures. (4) The task is large: the runner may land it in slices (design doc, transport plus the read and render tools, then tool areas one by one, then the scenarios), keeping this task open and logging progress, or split the remaining areas into tasks sequenced right behind it, each still p1 and source user. (5) A runner cannot drive Claude Code against the real app on a locked screen if the transport needs the screen; say which in the design. (6) Never put Claude or Anthropic in user-facing app copy (repo rule); the skill and server are developer-facing and may name them.
acceptance: Design first, in docs/design/agent-mcp.md: how the server reaches the app (a running Photonz, launched if needed), the tool list grouped by area (history, documents, layers, text, shapes and paths, annotations and measurements, video timeline, zooms, transitions, titles, Library components, export, undo), how each tool maps onto the commands the app already runs, and why. Every edit goes through the same undoable history the UI uses, so one Command Z in the app undoes one Claude step

Seeing the work: tools that return the document as it currently stands, a structured read (layers, their frames, text, styles, the timeline with clips, times and transitions) AND a rendered image (a PNG of the canvas, optionally one layer or one region; for video, a frame at a time, or a contact sheet of frames across a range). Claude uses these to check what it made, so the skill tells it to look after each meaningful step

Full coverage is measured, not claimed: a test lists every command the app can run (menus, panels, right-click menus) and fails for each one that has no MCP tool, with an explicit list of the ones left out on purpose and why. The audit gives the count

The server installs with one command (it is registered with Claude Code as a plugin or an mcp config entry), and the skill ships with it in this repo, saying when to use which tool, the house look (consistent layout, spacing, the app's own title and transition styles), and the look-then-fix loop

Scenario 1, try path: with five recordings in History, ask Claude: 'I made 5 clips in my history. Take the last 5, and create a video montage which has a title page, and subtitle pages per clip with nice consistent layout and transitions. I want to see clips with recommended zooms. Each subtitle should show Case N where n is the clip number (1 through 5)'. The result is one video document: a title page, then for each clip a subtitle page reading Case 1 to Case 5 followed by the clip with the app's recommended zooms applied, the same layout and transition throughout, exported to an MP4. A contact sheet and the MP4 go in queue/audits/

Scenario 2, try path: 'Create a product icon svg of a box inside of a cloud.' Claude builds it from real shapes and paths in a Photonz document (not a pasted SVG string) and exports an SVG; the SVG and a render go in the audit

Scenario 3, try path: with a UI screenshot open in the app, 'annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements'. Claude reads the picture, finds the major elements, and places the app's own measurement annotations (sizes and gaps) on them, editable afterwards like any hand-made one. Before and after pictures go in the audit, with how many measurements were placed and whether each lands on a real edge (measured against the pixels, not eyeballed)

Scenario 4, try path: give Claude a website URL and ask it to build out the components it sees and recreate the design system, then rebuild a second website in that design language. Claude creates the design system (colours, type, spacing) and the components as Photonz Library components, then composes the second site's pages from those same components. Screenshots of the source site, the components and the rebuilt pages go in the audit

Each scenario runs from a fresh Claude Code session with only the skill and the server, recorded as a transcript in the audit. A scenario that cannot finish names the missing tool or app capability, and that gap is filed as its own task
Unit tests cover the server's tool schemas and the mapping from each tool to an app command; Scripts/test.sh passes

An audit under queue/audits/ with all four scenarios' outputs, the coverage count, and a decision card linking the montage MP4 and the icon so the user judges the look. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: manager pass 2026-10-19: split into four slices that claim first, in order: an-agent-can-reach-the-running-app-read-the-open (channel, read, picture), every-command-in-the-app-s-menus-can-be-run-by-n (every menu command by name, coverage test), then an-agent-can-draw-a-picture-with-shapes-paths-te (pictures, scenarios 2 and 3) and an-agent-can-cut-a-video-from-history-clips-with (video, scenario 1). This task now waits on them and finishes the ask: the skill, scenario 4 (a website design system rebuilt as Library components), all four scenarios rerun from a fresh session, the coverage count and the decision card. Its checklist is unchanged; items the slices already met are checked off by pointing at their audits. Epic moved to agent-skills, whose success list is these scenarios.
